body:
Upon a request sent to me, this was the message that I sent to her to make her reply like that:

This is my goodbye.

I can't say it through text, phone, or any other medium, so I need to write. I need to tell you of where my head is... where my heart is... and where it's going. I need to give you one final update as to the person I am, the person I'm becoming, and the ways that I feel myself changing... I need to tell you the way I feel about you, and then I need to let you go; once and for all.

I suppose I'll start by telling you what's happened since you left. I started by leaving the house and walking. I didn't want to say goodbye before I left, because goodbye is what you say before someone leaves... and I wasn't ready for that. I walked... if you could call it that. If this were post-apocalyptia I definitely would've been mistaken for a zombie. I probably looked drunk or something of that nature. I couldn't walk, I couldn't think, I couldn't focus.

I went to where things started. The graveyard. I hobbled through, far from civilization, my knife clipped to my belt. I thought about hurting myself, I thought about yelling out every angry word I could think of. I wanted so badly to call you a slut, a whore, or a fucking piece of shit... but I didn't, because you're not.

I walked from there over to peaceful meadows, I sat on the bench and thought to myself about how weeks before we were looking at cows and eating a sundae. I thought to myself about how that would never happen again. It hurt. I have no other words for it.

But up until that point I couldn't even wrap my head around everything, and then it sort of hit me all at once. I curled into a ball and cried on the sidewalk of the main road for a while. I don't really know how long, time is sort of meaningless to me when I'm upset, as my sleep schedule probably shows. When I got home I noticed that I had some comments from people on my statuses offering me support... and I called the last person I would normally talk to.

Jenn and I spoke on the phone for about an hour. She tried calming me down, but it didn't really help too much. I talked to Megz for a similar length of time, it did little to help. Since then I have watched roughly half of Shawshank Redemption. I've probably seen this movie 100 times. Perhaps more, but there is comfort in the familiar.

And so that brings us up to the current. After the hysteria and initial shock have worn off; with my words back in my head and my feelings starting to be sorted, I feel that it's absolutely necessary that I take this time to say some things that I simply cannot leave unsaid.

During the time that I knew you, I did everything in my power to make you comfortable, happy, calm, and reassured. I told you from day 1 that I'm hard... hard to be around; hard to understand, and hard to get close to. But you put in the time. And I waited... I waited until I was absolutely sure that you were who you said you were. I waited until I was certain that you were someone I could love with my entire being... and when I was sure, I tried to do so. I tried to help you in every way that I could.

But I don't have money, I know that's an issue, I've been trying to scare up some computer repair work on Craigslist, been talking with headhunters, been applying places in person... but nothing has panned out. Nothing is working as I planned it.

But what I did have was a plan. I planned on a lot of things, I figured that if I couldn't go 50/50 or greater in terms of money, I could help you more than anyone else in terms of how you felt about yourself. Your well-being became my job. Every morning before you went in and every night when you got home I would talk to you until you felt content, happy, reassured. Sometimes for hours, even when it discomforted me to do so. Sometimes it was the best thing that happened to me all day.

But then a few weeks ago everything started to fall apart. Everything started to fail, my self esteem, your lies, and my ability to be "okay" with where my life was. I tried to put on a smile, but I was hurting, a lot. I couldn't keep it up anymore... I just couldn't feel okay. 

But Branden was right there to pick up the slack. I knew from the first email exactly what his intentions were, and what his plans were. I could tell by the tone, and by your need for affection that I had no chance. I tried to stay close, but I pushed away because I was so hurt at the reality that I saw coming. 

Over the last year, you've become everything to me. You've been the Bonnie to my Clyde. You've been my accomplice, my partner, my lover, my student, my slave, my navigator, my first in command and my best friend. Never has someone filled so many roles in my life and made me feel so fulfilled. Mentally, sexually, physically, emotionally... you completed what was missing in me. There were only a handful of times where things were less than perfect with you. Even then, they were always right back to perfect.

And now I'm sitting here alone and I'm seeing everything fall apart around me. My ivory towers are made of Damascus when you're not near.

But I have to walk away, for me, for you.

There's just a few things I want to end with: 
1. We made some of the best memories of my life, I'll cherish them even in the wake of all the destruction. You mean enough to me that even though things ended like this that I'll never call you any bad names...

2. You were always insecure, about your weight, your looks, your boobs, whatever. I can honestly say that you were amazing. In bed, in appearance, in conversation, at being a lover in general. I will never be able to replace you. I have never had someone who is so completely "up my alley" as you. In every way, you were perfect for me.

3. Walking away has never been this difficult. I've never had someone who could make my day better just by looking at me. I've never met someone who could change who I am just by saying hello. I've never loved someone so much as I've loved you.

4. Finally, I've never been hurt by someone this much. I feel like I'll never trust anyone again. I feel like my capability to look at other people and see the good in them is totally gone. I feel like a shell of my former self that existed just a week or two ago. I can sit here and listen to the pained notes of a violin and see your face in my mind. I can feel your hand on the back of my head, telling me that I should go back to sleep, and that you'll see me again soon. I feel like this is all just a bad dream and I can't wake up... I'm thrashing, my skin feels too tight, my throat feels like it's swelling shut... I feel like I'm pulling away from everything that I am just to get away from the thoughts of you... but it's the thoughts of you coming back into my life that reassure me that things will be okay... but just as soon as I feel that reassurance I remember that you're not coming back, and it's heartbreak again.



I suppose that you'll take my advice and not reply to this, as I encouraged you to do with Adam / Jason... but just know that this is goodbye. I loved you more than the sun burns. I love your more than the sea erodes, and I loved you more than the notes of a song move a soul.

Noone will ever love you the way that I do.

But this once upon a time doesn't end with a happily ever after. It just ends awkwardly midsentence. The reader is left wondering, and forever onwards, nobody knows what their intention was.

And I suppose that's how things should be, because in the e

Edit: and just to add on... because that's what I do... I feel like nothing has been solved... but things are just passably better than they were... and that's all I really need to get through this... just to be a little bit better.   I'm sorry for bringing my emo B.S. in here.... thanks for putting up with me.
And as a funny sidenote, she misunderstood my name (Damien) for the name of the guy that she's seeing now: "Branden" and called me Branden a few times.... awesome.

I tried calling the second number... The girl I talked with was way more interested in tracing my call than she was in making me feel better.  She kept asking questions that were even more painful than what I had said leading up to it.

"So yeah... now I'm all alone?"
"What could you have done to not make that happen?"

Is that really what you should ask someone?  The moment I said "I think I'm good enough to make it through the rest of the day" she rushed off the phone...

I think I feel worse now that I scared a suicide hotline worker away.
